# 5 Things to Consider When Choosing a New Home Location


Tri Pointe Homes


•


September 30, 2026


Share this article


Choosing a new home is also a decision about where you want your life to unfold. The coffee shop you stop by on Saturday morning. The route you take to work. The trail you return to again and again. The places you rely on and the ones you simply enjoy having close by.


At Tri Pointe Homes®, where we build starts with how people want to live. As you explore our new home communities, these five questions can help you think beyond the map and consider how a location might complement the life you want to lead.


## **1. What do you want your everyday routine to look like?**


Start with the stops that fill an ordinary week: grocery stores, healthcare providers, schools, fitness studios and other essentials. Which do you visit most often, and which would you appreciate having just a short trip from home?


Walk through a typical day, from morning errands to evening activities. You may value several destinations close together or prefer a quieter setting and be comfortable traveling farther. Identifying those preferences can help you compare locations in practical terms.


At[Twinleaf Townes in Chapel Hill, North Carolina](https://www.tripointehomes.com/nc/raleigh/twinleaf-townes?utm_medium=publications&utm_source=tphblog&utm_campaign=tphbrand_blog_findyourplace) , modern townhomes put shopping, dining and outdoor recreation within reach, with nearby destinations including The Streets at Southpoint, Meadowmont and the American Tobacco Trail. Think about how those surroundings could fit into your week, whether you’re picking up dinner or making time for an evening walk.


If schools are part of your search, confirm current boundaries, enrollment requirements and transportation information directly with the appropriate district, as these details are subject to change.


## **2. How close do you want to be to the action?**


For some home shoppers, there’s an undeniable appeal to the energy of a city. Restaurants, arts and entertainment, and lively gathering places can all contribute to its character. Others appreciate a slower pace, with the option to seek out that energy when they choose.


If you’re exploring the Charlotte area,[Ross Farms in Ballantyne, North Carolina](https://www.tripointehomes.com/nc/charlotte/ross-farms?utm_medium=publications&utm_source=tphblog&utm_campaign=tphbrand_blog_findyourplace) , pairs low-maintenance townhome living with a location near shopping, dining and entertainment, including events and activities at The Bowl at Ballantyne. It’s an opportunity to consider how a favorite dinner spot or a local event could become part of your routine.


After you tour a Tri Pointe Homes community, spend time in the surrounding area. Walk through a nearby downtown, browse local shops or settle in for lunch. Notice the activity around you, from busy sidewalks and outdoor dining to quieter streets.


A weekday morning and a weekend evening may offer different impressions. Experiencing both can help you decide whether the area’s pace suits you.


## **3. Where do you want to spend your time outdoors?**


Your ideal day outdoors might start on a trail, unfold near the water or include a relaxed afternoon at the park.


Look at the landscape surrounding a prospective community and the activities it offers. Coastlines, lakes, foothills, desert scenery, parks and trail networks each create different opportunities to get outside. Which would you use regularly, and which would be an occasional getaway?


For those drawn to the coast,[EvenTide in New Smyrna Beach, Florida](https://www.tripointehomes.com/fl/orlando/eventide?utm_medium=publications&utm_source=tphblog&utm_campaign=tphbrand_blog_findyourplace) , offers thoughtfully designed three-story townhomes near the Atlantic shoreline. With opportunities to explore the beach and kayak the Indian River, the surrounding area invites you to imagine more time by the water, whether that means a morning along the shore or a weekend on the river.


As you explore, check practical details such as operating hours, seasonal conditions, fees, parking and access requirements. These can help you understand what it would take to enjoy your favorite activities throughout the year.


## **4. Where will you need to go beyond the neighborhood?**


A home’s location also shapes how you connect to the wider area, whether you’re getting to work, reaching an airport, visiting family or heading out for the weekend.


Identify the trips you expect to make most often and the transportation options available. Major roadways, rail lines and public transportation may each play a role, depending on your destinations.


At[Avondale in Fate, Texas](https://www.tripointehomes.com/tx/dallas-fort-worth/avondale-dfw?utm_medium=publications&utm_source=tphblog&utm_campaign=tphbrand_blog_findyourplace) , a location near Rockwall offers connections to the Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex via major routes including I-30 and President George Bush Turnpike. For home shoppers seeking small-town surroundings while staying connected to the broader region, it’s a setting worth exploring.


At[Northpark Towns in North Bethesda, Maryland](https://www.tripointehomes.com/md/montgomery/northpark-towns?utm_medium=publications&utm_source=tphblog&utm_campaign=tphbrand_blog_findyourplace) , thoughtfully designed townhomes sit four blocks from the North Bethesda Metro Station, with access to I-270 and I-495. Shopping, dining and entertainment at Pike & Rose are also within walking distance. It’s a setting that invites you to consider how having several ways to get around could complement your routine, from a train ride into Washington, D.C., to dinner closer to home.


When possible, travel likely routes at the times you’d actually use them. A commute during rush hour can offer a different perspective from a midday drive. Traffic, construction, transit schedules and weather can also affect travel time.


If planned roads, businesses or public improvements factor into your search, consult official local sources for the latest information and keep in mind that future development plans may change.


## **5. Which priorities matter most to you?**


As you compare locations, you may find that each offers a different balance. One might put you closer to work, while another offers easier access to the outdoor activities you enjoy. Sometimes, what matters most is what you can experience within the community itself.


At[Atwell in Banning, California](https://www.tripointehomes.com/ca/riverside-county/atwell?utm_medium=publications&utm_source=tphblog&utm_campaign=tphbrand_blog_findyourplace) , neighborhood walking trails along historic Smith Creek, pools and playgrounds create opportunities to spend time outdoors close to home. If a neighborhood stroll or an afternoon at the pool is high on your list, community amenities may deserve as much consideration as the destinations beyond them.


Separate your must-haves from the features that would be nice to have. A manageable commute may be essential, while being minutes from a favorite restaurant may be a preference you’re willing to trade for something else.


Consider how those priorities might evolve, too. Would the location still work if your schedule changed, you traveled more often or you took up a new hobby?


Return to your list after each community visit. Knowing where you’re flexible and what matters most can help you make a confident decision.


## **Find a Place That Fits Your Life**


The right home starts with a location that feels right for you. From beachside surroundings and neighborhood trails to nearby dining and city connections, the places around your home help shape the way you live.


[Explore Tri Pointe Homes communities across the country](https://www.tripointehomes.com/find-your-home?utm_medium=publications&utm_source=tphblog&utm_campaign=tphbrand_blog_findyourplace) and discover a setting that brings you closer to what matters most.
